dish.name: Arisi Paruppu Sadam
dish.description: A comforting one-pot rice and lentil staple native to the Kongu Nadu region of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.

ingredients.name: Coriander leaves (Koththamalli)
ingredients.looksLike: Fresh finely chopped green herb leaves

steps.title: Rinse the rice and lentil together.
steps.text: Measure 60 g raw rice and 30 g toor dal into a bowl. Wash thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear.
steps.cameraCheck: Ensure clear visibility of the bowl contents.
steps.funFact: Arisi Paruppu Sadam is an iconic comforting dish native to the Kongu Nadu region.
steps.tip: Use short-grain Ponni rice for authentic regional texture.
steps.videoShot: Top-down view of rice and dal being rinsed.
steps.visualCue: The rinsing water turns translucent after three washes.
steps.watchOut: Avoid rubbing too vigorously or grains can shatter into fragments.

steps.title: Soak the washed grains.
steps.text: Pour enough clean water to submerge the rice and dal completely. Set the bowl aside for 20 minutes.
steps.cameraCheck: Focus on the bowl resting on the kitchen counter.
steps.tip: Pre-soaking ensures rapid uniform softening inside the pressure vessel.
steps.videoShot: Side angle close-up of water covering grains.
steps.visualCue: Lentil kernels swell noticeably and lighten in shade.
steps.watchOut: Do not soak past 30 minutes to prevent overly soft texture.

steps.title: Prep the aromatics.
steps.text: Peel and coarsely chop 30 g shallots and 10 g garlic. Chop 40 g ripe tomato into small cubes.
steps.cameraCheck: Show the board with properly diced aromatics.
steps.tip: Small Indian shallots yield superior local sweetness over regular onions.
steps.videoShot: Overhead shot of chopping onions and garlic.
steps.visualCue: Shallots and tomatoes rest chopped in neat uniform bits.
steps.watchOut: Avoid paper-thin onion slices which scorch too rapidly.

steps.title: Heat ghee in the pressure cooker.
steps.text: Place a small 3-litre pressure cooker on medium heat and add 10 ml ghee.
steps.cameraCheck: Frame the bottom interior of the open cooker.
steps.tip: Ghee unlocks a rich traditional aroma unattainable with plain oil.
steps.videoShot: Medium shot of pouring ghee into warmed cooker.
steps.visualCue: The ghee melts fully and shimmers lightly across the base.
steps.watchOut: Do not let cooker overheat to smoking point before tempering.

steps.title: Crackle the spices.
steps.text: Add 2 g mustard seeds, 2 g cumin seeds, 1 dry red chilli, and 5 curry leaves. Sizzle gently.
steps.cameraCheck: Close-up on crackling seasonings at bottom.
steps.tip: Snapping the red chilli exposes seeds for deeper background warmth.
steps.videoShot: Macro view of spluttering mustard and cumin seeds.
steps.visualCue: Mustard seeds pop merrily while curry leaves crisp up.
steps.watchOut: If seasonings turn black instantly, discard and lower the stove heat.

steps.title: Sauté the shallots and garlic.
steps.text: Toss in chopped shallots and garlic into the hot fat. Fry for 2 minutes until translucent.
steps.cameraCheck: Ensure lighting captures glistening translucent onion pieces.
steps.tip: Stir steadily so garlic browns evenly without dark edges.
steps.videoShot: Pan-level shot stirring shallots with garlic.
steps.visualCue: Shallots soften into light pink translucent morsels.
steps.watchOut: Burnt garlic ruins the pot base with lingering bitter undertones.

steps.title: Cook tomatoes with spice powders.
steps.text: Add chopped tomatoes, 1 g turmeric powder, 2 g sambar powder, and 3 g salt. Cook down until mushy.
steps.cameraCheck: Show tomato mix softening into a smooth jam.
steps.tip: Press tomatoes using spoon back to speed up crushing.
steps.videoShot: Close-up shot of stirring spices into tomatoes.
steps.visualCue: Tomatoes collapse into a thick fragrant spiced paste.
steps.watchOut: Keep flame low so dried spice powders do not scorch.

steps.title: Pour water and bring to boil.
steps.text: Drain soaked rice and dal thoroughly. Add 250 ml water into the cooker base and heat to rolling boil.
steps.cameraCheck: Capture liquid bubbling vigorously across the base.
steps.tip: Tasting boiling liquid allows salt correction before closing lid.
steps.videoShot: Angle shot of pouring water into cooker pot.
steps.visualCue: Energetic boiling bubbles stream rapidly across the pan surface.
steps.watchOut: Skimping on water ratio leaves central grains chalky and dry.

steps.title: Mix in soaked grains and seal.
steps.text: Transfer drained rice and dal into boiling broth and mix once. Lock cooker lid with weight fitted.
steps.cameraCheck: Show cooker lid turning securely into locked state.
steps.tip: One quick stir stops heavy rice from settling at base.
steps.videoShot: Medium shot of securing lid and positioning whistle.
steps.visualCue: Steam escapes softly in steady bursts through top vent line.
steps.watchOut: Ensure rubber lid ring is seated tightly before sealing.

steps.title: Cook for three whistles.
steps.text: Cook on medium heat for 3 whistles, lasting around 8 minutes. Turn off stove burner immediately.
steps.cameraCheck: Keep upper pressure cooker whistle centered in frame.
steps.tip: Tracking whistle counts yields perfectly cooked, soft intact grains.
steps.videoShot: Wide shot capturing steam release from cooker whistle.
steps.visualCue: Whistle rises loudly while spouting thick cloud columns.
steps.watchOut: Avoid high heat settings which burn bottom layer grains.

steps.title: Allow natural pressure release.
steps.text: Leave pressure cooker untouched for 10 minutes until steam depressurizes completely on its own.
steps.cameraCheck: Focus on the cooker safety valve mechanism.
steps.tip: Trapped residual heat cooks inner lentil cores to creamy perfection.
steps.videoShot: Still shot watching safety pin lower fully down.
steps.visualCue: Safety weight pin drops completely indicating depressurized interior.
steps.watchOut: Forcing lid open prematurely causes uneven half-cooked grains.

steps.title: Fluff and garnish.
steps.text: Unseal lid carefully, stir gently using a fork, and sprinkle 5 g chopped fresh coriander leaves.
steps.cameraCheck: Focus inside opened vessel revealing steaming yellow rice.
steps.tip: Adding extra fresh ghee at finish boosts regional flavor profiles.
steps.videoShot: Top-down view fluffing bright yellow steam rice.
steps.visualCue: Rice looks moist, fully tender, fluffy, and vibrant yellow.
steps.watchOut: Do not stir aggressively while hot to avoid mushy paste.

dish.batchNote: Scales up easily in a 5-litre pressure cooker up to 4 servings without changing total whistling times.
dish.storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; reheat thoroughly with a sprinkle of water.
